articles.summary: Discover how WWE superstar Bianca Belair transformed her impressive wrestling success into a thriving financial empire through endorsements, fashion ventures, and entertainment projects.
articles.body: Bianca Belair has developed from a rising WWE performer into one of the company’s most recognisable women’s wrestling stars. Her athletic background, distinctive “EST” persona and major championship moments have helped establish a brand that extends well beyond match results. That growing visibility has also created opportunities in merchandise, sponsorships, fashion and entertainment.According to Celebrity Net Worth, Bianca Belair’s estimated net worth is between $3 million and $5 million, with several 2026 reports placing the figure around $4 million. WWE does not publicly disclose the complete compensation packages of individual performers, meaning salary, bonuses, merchandise royalties and other earnings can vary.Bianca Belair’s growing fortune reflects WWE successBelair’s financial growth has closely followed her rise inside WWE. After entering the company’s developmental system, she became a major fixture of its women’s division and eventually established herself as a championship-level performer.Her breakthrough came with the 2021 Women’s Royal Rumble victory, which led to her WrestleMania 37 main-event match against Sasha Banks. The historic bout made Belair one of the most prominent names in WWE’s women’s division and strengthened her commercial profile.Her championship résumé has continued to add value to that profile. Belair became the longest-reigning Raw Women’s Champion with a 420-day reign, while her later Women’s Tag Team Championship victory with Jade Cargill helped make her a WWE Women’s Triple Crown Champion.Bianca Belair expands earnings beyond wrestlingWWE remains the foundation of Belair’s income, but her commercial opportunities have become increasingly important. Her merchandise presence, premium live event appearances, licensing opportunities and sponsorship work provide potential revenue streams beyond a standard wrestling contract.WWE performers can receive compensation from several sources, including merchandise, appearances, licensing and event-related bonuses. Because individual contracts are generally private, publicly reported salary estimates should be treated as estimates rather than confirmed figures.Belair has also been connected with brands including C4 Energy, Fenty Beauty, DraftKings and Slim Jim in recent reporting. WWE and C4 announced their partnership with Belair among the company's featured athletes in 2021, demonstrating how her fitness-focused image translated naturally into commercial campaigns.Bianca Belair builds a powerful media brandBelair’s biggest advantage outside the ring is the recognisable identity she has created around her WWE character. Her signature look, elaborate entrances and distinctive ring gear have become important parts of her public image.She personally designs and makes much of her wrestling gear, a skill that began developing seriously before becoming an important part of her WWE presentation. Her fashion work has included creating gear for herself and for her husband, fellow WWE performer Montez Ford. She has also discussed ambitions of eventually taking her fashion interests further.That creative identity has helped Belair stand apart in an increasingly commercial WWE environment. Her look can translate into merchandise, promotional campaigns, video games, television appearances and other forms of entertainment.Her media footprint expanded further with “Love & WWE: Bianca & Montez,” the Hulu reality series featuring Belair and Montez Ford, and WWE confirmed the show's launch in 2023, while the series gave viewers a behind-the-scenes look at their professional and personal lives.The combination of championship credibility, a distinctive fashion identity, sponsorship appeal and television exposure has therefore given Belair several avenues for continued commercial growth. articles.summary: Justin Boone takes you through his top fantasy football waiver wire options for Week 5.
articles.body:
Every Monday during the season, Justin Boone breaks down the recommended waiver-wire pickups.

Brissett hasn't picked up where he left off last season, when he was a top-10 fantasy quarterback on a per game basis over the final 12 games. Fortunately, a matchup with the banged-up Lions secondary is the perfect recipe for any passer.

Through four weeks, Detroit has allowed at least 20 fantasy points to every quarterback the unit has faced, including Tyler Shough (QB6 in Week 1), Josh Allen (QB1 in Week 2), Geno Smith (QB3 in Week 3) and Bryce Young (QB6 in Week 4 with only Monday Night Football remaining).

Brissett is an excellent streaming option this week, just be careful about expecting any long-term solutions from him. Arizona will take on the Broncos, Rams (twice), Seahawks and Chiefs in five of the next six outings. If Brissett struggles and continues to turn the ball over (three interceptions this week), the Cardinals will likely see what they have in rookie Carson Beck down the stretch.

Sam Darnold i s 53% rostered but would be the No. 2 QB add behind Stroud, if available.

With Jadarian Price being placed on injured reserve, Wilson became a priority add in the lead up to Week 4. He answered the call with 21 carries for 81 rushing yards and a touchdown, as well as another 39 yards and a receiving TD on three receptions.

That's a better spot start than any fantasy manager could have hoped for, but the Seahawks' backfield is constantly evolving week to week. The latest wrinkle came in the form of a brief flirtation with Joe Mixon. After planning to sign Mixon, the front office changed it's mind after his physical. The Seahawks did add more depth by signing rookie Robert Henry Jr. off the Commanders' practice squad.

We still don't know when Zach Charbonnet will be activated, but his practice window opened last week. Head coach Mike Macdonald said that Charbonnet won't play in Week 5, so we continue to monitor his status. Seattle's frantic attempt to add multiple backs over the last few days does make you wonder about Charbonnet's recovery timeline.

This all boils down to at least one more start for Wilson and possibly more until Charbonnet gets involved. Sadly, the end result here is heading towards some sort of committee in the second half of the season, which will limit the ceilings of every Seattle back.

The trainer's room is a busy place in Philadelphia, with DeVonta Smith and Dallas Goedert ruled out for Week 4, and Saquon Barkley joining them on the sidelines during the game due to a hamstring injury.

Bigsby handled the majority of the work from that point on, totaling 55 yards on 14 carries in the loss with Shipley being the preferred passing-down back. To complicate the situation even more, Bigsby left the game late in the fourth quarter with an injury of his own and now is reportedly headed for an IR stint .

The initial updates on Barkley suggest it's not a serious injury, but any hamstring ailment can result in a missed game or two. For the time being, Shipley needs to be a priority add in case Barkley can't suit up next week, even though the Jaguars' run defense isn't an ideal opponent for a spot start on Sunday.

If Barkley is out, Shipley will be a fantasy RB3 with low-end RB2 upside given the banged up state of the offense. In that scenario, the Eagles would likely elevate either Dameon Pierce or Jaydon Blue from their practice squad to back him up.

Despite saving his fantasy day yet again with a touchdown, Omarion Hampton's usage continues to trend in the wrong direction. This week, the three-man committee played nearly even snaps with Mitchell (26), Hampton (25) and Kimani Vidal (25) sharing the backfield.

Hampton still led the way in fantasy production by turning his 11 touches into 53 scrimmage yards and a score, but Mitchell saw the most volume overall with 15 touches and 63 yards. Even Vidal had a solid outing with 36 yards and a receiving TD on seven chances.

This type of deployment makes it difficult to project usage and stat lines for the Chargers backs on a weekly basis. However, it's clear Mitchell is a favorite of offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel, who reportedly pounded the table to add him in the offseason. Given Mitchell's uptick in volume and gamebreaking speed, he should be picked up as an upside RB3/flex to see how this develops in the coming weeks.

Woody Marks is 55% rostered but would be the No. 3 RB add behind Wilson and Bigsby, if available.

Best one-injury away backup RBs to stash

Chris Rodriguez Jr. vs. PHI (37% rostered)

Washington has become a regular part of the waiver wire column, since he still remains available in almost 70% of leagues. That's despite averaging 55 receiving yards per game through the opening month.

Now, the 25-year-old is coming off his best outing of the season with five catches and 67 yards against the Vikings. He's also earned target shares of 28% and 29% over the last two weeks, which is especially important in Miami's low-volume passing attack.

This isn't a league-winning waiver wire pickup, but Washington can be a solid WR3/flex in your lineup as bye weeks begin.

This isn't the first time we've seen DJ Moore leave a game due to injury, only to have Coleman step up. The first time that occurred was in Week 2, when Coleman posted 63 yards and six receptions. On Sunday, the results were even better with Coleman catching six of his seven targets for 116 yards and a touchdown.

It's a one-game sample, but this was the best version of Coleman I can remember watching as a Bills fan. He looked more crisp on his routes and was getting some snaps out of the slot.

Coleman's path to being a star disappeared a long time ago, but he's now shown us on two separate occasions that he can fill in when injuries require it. While there weren't many silver linings to take away from this loss for Buffalo, Coleman's performance was a positive step towards him being a more capable second or third option in the offense.

For fantasy, you're picking him up in case Moore's aggravation leads to missed time. I'll update this article when we get an update on his status.

Even before Ladd McConkey aggravated his foot injury, Harris had taken on a bigger role in the Chargers offense this year. The 24-year-old wideout has topped 50 yards in each of his last three games while playing 77% of the snaps on the year. That includes a season-high 93% snap share in Week 4 when McConkey left early.

Harris now has 13 catches for 209 yards on 21 targets through four games. He's outproduced Quentin Johnston, who has just seven catches for 108 yards.

Investing in the Chargers' passing attack might not seem that exciting given Justin Herbert's struggles so far, but Harris is a low-risk pickup capable of returning fantasy WR3 value if McConkey sits out.

The market for Hill is reportedly heating up , with many people connecting the dots to his former team the Chiefs. Kansas City just lost Rashee Rice (short-term) and Tyquan Thornton (long-term) to injury, which creates a clear need at the position.

However, let's make one thing clear: this is not prime Tyreek Hill. Even prior to suffering a torn ACL, left knee dislocation and multiple other torn ligaments, the 32-year-old was a declining player.

Even so, if he's healthy and lands on a contender like the Chiefs, he could return fantasy WR3 value with some potential upside. This is still a stash and see situation, so don't let your expectations run wild until we find out where he signs and whether he's anywhere close to his past form.

The Bengals lost both their star wideouts to injuries on Sunday. Ja'Marr Chase's status is up in the air as he'll try to clear concussion protocol this week. Meanwhile, Tee Higgins is dealing with an adductor injury that's put him on the doubtful side to suit up in Week 5.

That allowed Meyers to see nine targets against the Jaguars, hauling in seven of them for 82 yards.

In their absence, Gesicki found the end zone for the third time this season. He now has three solid stat lines in four games, with 5-78-1, 3-37-1 and 3-40-1.

This week also marks a revenge game for Gesicki against the Dolphins. In his last meeting with Miami, he scored a touchdown as well. If both Chase and Higgins are sidelined, Gesicki will be a fantasy TE1 this week. If Chase manages to play, Gesicki will still be a strong high-end TE2 streamer.

Herbert has yet to reach 14 fantasy points in a single game this season. He's also been held to 226 passing yards or less and hasn't accounted for more than one touchdown in any outing. There are far better options at quarterback.

Kyler Murray wasn't able to take advantage of the Dolphins matchup and hasn't looked particularly good in his starts this season. He's also not as effective as a runner, with 17 rushing yards being his season high.

When he returns, this backfield will look completely different with Zach Charbonnet eventually returning and the team flirting with free agents. At best, Price will be locked in a committee in the second half of the season, which limits his potential in Year 1.

articles.title: NFL Week 5 Power Rankings Round-up 2026: Raiders hold ground after loss
articles.summary: The Raiders kept respect in the power rankings for Week 5 despite loss to the Chiefs.
articles.body:
In week four the Las Vegas Raiders lost to the Chiefs, but were in a neck-and-neck battle for much of the contest, proving that their hot start to the season start is for real. Despite Kirk Cousins going for 365 passing yards and two passing touchdowns, Brock Bowers going for 86 receiving yards and Michael Mayer going for 82 receiving yards, Las Vegas was unable to come away with the win.

Chiefs running back Kenneth Walker III went for 177 rushing yards and two rushing touchdowns, and Tyquan Thornton went for 111 receiving yards and two touchdowns, helping Kansas City win their fourth game of the year and remain undefeated.

Las Vegas is still firmly in the playoff mix, with a 3-1 record heading into Week 5. Their status among the contending teams in the league did not greatly diminish, as they showed they were capable of giving the Chiefs a great fight. After earning an average power ranking of 10.8 following Week 3, let's round up some power rankings and see how the Raiders are viewed heading into Week 3.

"Where has this franchise been? Andy Reid has the most wins (7) of any coach − including the Raiders' − at Allegiant Stadium. And while Klint Kubiak's troops arguably legitimized themselves by nearly knocking off Reid's Chiefs on Sunday, they'll be challenged to keep it up − the Patriots, Bills, Rams, 49ers, Seahawks and Broncos are among the Silver and Black's next seven opponents."

Chad Graff and Josh Kendall, The Athletic — 13

"The Raiders lost, but they've got to come away from Sunday's game feeling pretty good. They've already matched their win total from a year ago. New coach Klint Kubiak is exceeding expectations, and even 38-year-old Kirk Cousins is slinging it. There's not a lot to be worried about in Vegas given what this season could've looked like."

"There are no moral victories here, but the Raiders sure have plenty to be proud of after their narrow Week 4 loss to Kansas City . The upstart Las Vegas squad battled with big brother for four quarters and nearly handed the Chiefs their first loss of 2026. Kirk Cousins is playing fantastically, and the defensive additions have helped transform the team from an also-ran into a squad that deserves a ton of respect. I'm not sure how the story will end, but I'm glad we're along for the ride."

"Even after the Raiders' heartbreaking loss to the Chiefs, there's a sense that first-time coach Klint Kubiak is building something special in Las Vegas. The Raiders were competitive for four quarters against Kansas City. They are better than expected and should be a competitive team each week, especially with quarterback Kirk Cousins playing at a high level. With the Chargers 0-4 and the Broncos 2-2, it's not crazy to suggest Las Vegas can make a playoff run in Year 1 of the Kubiak era."

"They lost for the first time Sunday, but they showed they are a good team by pushing the Chiefs. At 3-1, they are one of the surprise teams in the league."

"Las Vegas outgained the Chiefs 437-398, which is of little consolation but shows Vegas was close to knocking off Kansas City. If anything, the Raiders validated their hot start with a close loss to a Chiefs team that is 4-0 and has won nine of the last 10 AFC West titles."

"While aggressive, the Raiders will miss the mark at times, but they're good enough to hang with the NFL's upper-echelon teams. Keep in mind that playoff-caliber clubs have a better chance of capitalizing on Las Vegas' mistakes."

"I don't know what happens from here, but the fact that the Raiders have gotten incredible production out of a handful of players the previous regime deemed unplayable—and are getting game-changing plays from a 2026 fifth-round pick in the secondary—have me more confident in the John Spytek-Tom Brady mind meld than I've ever been."

The Raiders approach another matchup against a Super Bowl contender in the New England Patriots next week. The Patriots secured a huge bounce back win against the Buffalo Bills in Week 4 and are now 2-2 after they were facing a potential 1-3 start to the year.

The Raiders' 3-0 season may quickly turn into a 3-2 record and a fight to have a comfortable advantage in the standings if they do not attack the Patriots and do what is necessary to win. New England is not on as nearly as good of a roll as Kansas City is at this juncture of the offseason, and the tight loss to the Chiefs is still a boost of morale heading into Week 5.

articles.title: Harry Kane equals England record, scores twice in 3-0 win over Czechia
articles.summary: England’s Harry Kane makes record-equalling 125th appearance and has a hand in all three goals in Nations League win.
articles.body:
Harry Kane celebrated his record-equalling 125th England cap with two trademark goals as Thomas Tuchel’s side cruised past Czechia 3-0 on Tuesday for their third straight Nations League win.

Captain Kane matched Peter Shilton’s men’s appearance record and went on to score his 90th and 91st international goals at Wembley as the home side ended the window in style.

England opened their Nations League campaign with a narrow 3-2 defeat to world champions Spain late last month before beating the Czechs 2-0 in Prague and hammering Croatia 7-0 .

Tuchel made four changes to the side that crushed Croatia at the weekend, resting the in-form Anthony Gordon and fellow winger Bukayo Saka.

Trent Alexander-Arnold returned at right-back for his first Wembley appearance for his country in two years and immediately looked at home.

The Real Madrid right-back forced a smart save from Czech goalkeeper Lukas Hornicek in the opening minutes with a sweetly struck free-kick after Morgan Rogers was brought down outside the box.

Chelsea forward Rogers was frequently at the heart of the action as England probed but they created few clear-cut chances against the limited visitors.

The deadlock was broken in bizarre fashion in the 27th minute when Czech defender Vladimir Coufal steered the ball into his own net from a Kane cross.

Manchester City midfielder Elliot Anderson went close to making it 2-0 moments later but skied his shot over the bar.

Bayern Munich forward Kane, a contender for the Ballon d’Or, gave the home crowd what they had been craving five minutes before half-time, finishing off a sweeping England move.

Anderson hit a first-time pass to Rogers wide on the right, who delivered first time into the box, into the path of the onrushing Kane.

The 33-year-old was inches away from a second in the early stages of the second half when he clipped the crossbar following another flowing England attack.

But the crowd did not have to wait long to hail England’s record goalscorer again – celebrating after he headed home at the back post from Lewis Hall’s corner in the 57th minute.

Tuchel made a number of changes but left Kane on as the forward hunted a hat-trick.

Kane was eventually brought off to a standing ovation with less than 10 minutes to go, hugged and slapped on the back by Tuchel as he was replaced by Dominic Calvert-Lewin.

The win leaves England strongly placed to secure a top-two spot in Group A3, which would take them into the Nations League quarterfinals in March.

They are on nine points after four games, three behind leaders Spain, who came from behind to beat Croatia 2-1 on Tuesday.

But the night belonged to Kane, who proved he is as sharp as ever, 11 years after scoring 79 seconds into his debut.

articles.title: WWE NXT Results, Winners, Live Grades, Reaction, Highlights From October 6
articles.summary: With Halloween Havoc quickly approaching, WWE NXT looks to lock in a compelling card for its next premium live event, even with nothing currently set in stone.
articles.body:
With Halloween Havoc quickly approaching, WWE NXT looks to lock in a compelling card for its next premium live event, even with nothing currently set in stone.

Kelani Jordan's NXT Women's Championship challenger at Halloween Havoc will be determined by way of a Battle Royal featuring talent across WWE, AAA and TNA. With champions such as Zaria and Xia Brookside involved, the outcome feels genuinely unpredictable.

Scores will also be settled as Shiloh Hill battles Naraku in a rematch from a few weeks back and Zilla Fatu fights Lexis King of BirthRight. Meanwhile, the Dusty Rhodes Tag Team Classic will continue when Hank and Tank take on Shido Ash and Viktor Zanov in first-round action.

Despite finding itself in a state of flux as of late, NXT has managed to keep the spotlight on the fresher faces and kill time until Halloween Havoc with interesting albeit brief programs and above-average action. The next several weeks of television will be imperative in making that show as strong as possible.

Here are the complete results, grades and reaction for the Oct. 6 edition of WWE NXT as it airs live on The CW.

Last Time in Action: BirthRight def. Zilla Fatu, EK Prosper and Sean Legacy (N XT, Sept. 22).

It was a competitive contest throughout with Lexis King taking it to Zilla Fatu early on and coming across as his equal, despite being booked as an undercard competitor for the better part of the past three years.

King caught Fatu with a flurry of kicks to the chest but was thwarted by an emphatic Samoan Drop from Fatu. A short while later, he laid out King with a diving headbutt in the corner before wiping out most of BirthRight on the apron and no-selling a superkick from King.

Fatu clinched the victory after dropping King with his signature Samoan Spike. BirthRight jumped Fatu afterward, sent him into the steel steps at ringside and used them to crush his hand.

NXT is definitely doing a better job of portraying BirthRight as more of a dominant force. Granted, the outcome of this contest was never in doubt, but at least King got some offense in before eating defeat.

Fatu is still early on in his NXT run but is already getting over nicely with this audience. It's also wise to keep him out of the NXT Championship picture for the foreseeable future as not to rush his development.

The post-match angle was effective in furthering the feud and allowing BirthRight to get his heat back. Don't be surprised to see Fatu run through other members of the group before he gets his hands on King again.

Dusty Classic First Round: Hank and Tank vs. Shido Ash and Viktor Zanov

Last Time in Action: Keanu Carver def. Tank Ledger (NXT, July 7); Carver def. Hank Walker (NXT, July 21); Shido Ash and Vikor Zanov's NXT TV in-ring debut.

Shido Ash and Viktor Zanov represented Evolve in this tournament. We heard from them briefly beforehand via a quick vignette where they explained their judo backgrounds, which served as a perfectly fine introduction to the team, but they didn't show much personality in their promo.

In the ring, though, they showed signs of potential. Their unique judo style did give them the advantage at various points, specifically down the stretch when they countered Hank and Tank's tag finisher and nearly upset the former NXT Tag Team champs with a swift takedown.

Hank and Tank pulled through, however, battling back from the adversity to put the newcomers away in decisive fashion.

Hank and Tank defeated Shido Ash and Viktor Zanov to advance to the quarterfinals of the Dusty Rhodes Tag Team Classic.

Ash and Zanov are obviously works in progress, but with this marking their NXT in-ring debut, they held their own and had a solid showing. The fact this wasn't booked as a straightforward squash is an encouraging sign for their future.

Hank and Tank have been spinning their wheels for quite some time and this served as a nice reminder of what they can do. That said, they have virtually no chance of getting past the quarterfinals with The Creed Brothers being their next opponents.

Grayson Waller Addresses His Successful NXT Championship Defense

One week removed from successfully defending the NXT Championship, Grayson Waller emerged to discuss how impressive EK Prosper was and the heart he showed in defeat last Tuesday night.

He also talked about wanting to make the NXT Championship matter again and getting it back to a point where title defenses feel as important as they once did. That brought out Myles Borne, who recently severed ties with Tavion Heights to cement his status as a heel.

Borne is done doing what's expected of him, he said, and he now his sights set on the one piece of gold in NXT he hasn't held yet. Tony D'Angelo then walked out to make it clear that he has unfinished business with the belt before explaining that he didn't answer the open challenge last week because he doesn't want Waller to have any excuses.

Waller told Borne and D'Angelo that he'll defend against whoever wins between the two of them next week. The segment ended with Borne laying out D'Angelo with a loaded fist and facing off with Waller.

Waller is always his annoying heel self in his promos, so it was notable when he said that Prosper "crushed it" against him last week. That was an awesome endorsement of Prosper's potential, along with Prosper's backstage interaction with William Regal later in the show.

Borne has a bit of momentum right now following his heel turn, despite losing both of his bouts at Heatwave in August. Borne vs. Waller isn't an interesting match on paper because of the heel vs. heel dynamic, so Heights costing Borne the win to further that feud would be logical.

It's a shame that whatever took Mason Rook out of action is going to prevent him from getting the shot he earned at the NXT Championship at Halloween Havoc, too. Waller vs. Rook will happen eventually, but NXT might be going in a different direction for right now in case Waller vs. Rook was supposed to be more than a one-off.

Now or Never for LA Knight, More Raw Fallout 🗣️

Last Time in Action: Naraku def. Shiloh Hill (NXT, Sept. 1).

This was a rematch from the Sept. 1 edition of NXT where Naraku beat Shiloh Hill after cheating with his mist.

Hill gradually built momentum in the early goings of this bout by planting Hill with a shoulder block. Naraku retaliated down the stretch with a powerful sit-out slam, but it wasn't enough to earn him the victory.

Hill kept the crowd behind him by hitting some of his signature stuff, including a reverse flipping senton. After blocking Naraku's mist, Hill ducked out of the way when Naraku went for it a second time, which resulted in the referee getting misted and calling for the bell.

Shiloh Hill defeated Naraku by disqualification.

We are now two matches into this feud and neither encounter has been overly exciting. Both guys are technically sound but don't have the strongest chemistry as opponents evidently.

The disqualification finish was fine as it avoided the usual formula of Hill avenging his previous loss to Naraku, but the execution could have been a bit better. The two brawling to the back after the match was over was underwhelming as well.

Needless to say, a third match is in order and it should have some sort of a stipulation to raise the stakes, perhaps something relating to the mist. The endgame of this program should ultimately be to elevate Hill to championship contention.

articles.title: LeBron James Battling Multiple Injuries Ahead of 76ers Season
articles.summary: LeBron James has reportedly been dealing with foot and back injures. A problem that could be reoccurring throughout the season.
articles.body:
The Philadelphia 76ers may have a problem on their hands.

As reported by ESPN, LeBron James is dealing with some left foot tendinitis as well as some pain with his sciatica. James dealt with the sciatica issue last season with the Los Angeles Lakers, and it seems to be a persistent problem heading into this season.

This was one of the biggest problems that many expected to see as James enters his 24th season at the age of 42. Until his stint with the Lakers, James was never a huge concern when it came to the injuries because he took such great care of his body. Now, it seems Father Time is starting to catch up to him. Things are okay for now because it's something the team can manage until the start of the season.

Now here's the big problem here: Both of these injuries are a huge concern because neither one can be completely cured. The hope is that they can keep it manageable and maybe it won't cause James to miss an extensive amount of time.

If James ends up missing time, this could cause a huge wrinkle in what the 76ers want to do with the team. There's already growing concern for this team with how so many players are already battling injuries and the season is two weeks away. The good thing is that the bench depth could provide a sigh of relief. Now, there's obviously no replacing a player the likes of James, but this team has enough to get by. Offensively, they shouldn't miss a beat.

Tyrese Maxey and Jaylen Brown alone can handle the offensive scoring . The concern could come on the defensive end. James may have lost a step on the defensive side, but his IQ makes up for that, and that's going to be the element that will be missed the most.

VJ Edgecombe and Joel Embiid, along with Brown, can handle things defensively, but it won't be without its share of hiccups. James was brought to this team to help get them over the hump of the second round of the playoffs. But if these two injuries keep him out of action, he may not be able to stop the storm from coming.

It's too early to declare that this team is in trouble, but with James having these kinds of problems, it's going to be hard to not criticize the 76ers and the problems that lie ahead.

articles.title: “Stop the Lies”: LeBron James Slams Report Claiming He Scolded Joel Embiid
articles.summary: 2 years ago, Tyrese Maxey called out Joel Embiid over a lack of accountability. So when a new report claimed LeBron James had also taken issue with his Olymp...
articles.body:
2 years ago, Tyrese Maxey called out Joel Embiid over a lack of accountability. So when a new report claimed LeBron James had also taken issue with his Olympian teammate, the connection was easy to make. But this time, the story may not be what it seemed. Bron has now pushed back on the report, suggesting the latest incident was never an issue at all.

During Monday's preseason game against the New York Knicks, longtime broadcaster Mike Breen revealed an interesting detail from the team's recent practices.

"They are, they're raving about how he's been so far. Obviously, it's only a week of camp. But I had somebody tell me before the game that they were out ready to practice and Joel Embiid walked out on the court a couple minutes late. LeBron let him hear it," Breen said.

LeBron James' Instagram Story now puts that account into question. He shared the 'ComplexSports' post, which had the caption, "LEBRON REPORTEDLY CHECKING EMBIID FOR BEING LATE."

"????!He ain't been late so stop the lies," wrote James .

The four-time champion did not simply ignore the report. He chose to address it himself, making it clear that his teammate had not been late during their time together. This matters because the original story quickly connected with an issue that has followed Embiid before.

During the 2024-25 season, Tyrese Maxey reportedly confronted Embiid during an hour-long team meeting after Philadelphia opened the season 2-11. Among the concerns raised was Embiid's punctuality. Maxey reportedly told his longtime teammate that he was late "for everything" and urged him to be on time for team activities.

Maxey later confirmed that he felt compelled to speak up during the difficult stretch.

"I wanted to speak up," Maxey said. "I felt the need to do that because I wanted to share that we are better than what we have shown on the floor. There was a lot said, but it is what it is. We said what we had to say and we have to figure out a way to move on to the rest of the season. Everyone understands what's at stake. Everyone is feeling the hurt."

Now, Breen's report once again raised questions about Joel Embiid's accountability. But LeBron James' response tells a different story.

The 22-time All-Star recently praised the 32-year-old center's health and availability. And even raved about his condition now and compared it with their time together on Team USA in 2024.

"The difference between '24 and now, he's just so much more healthy. He hasn't missed a practice. He's been in damn near everything that we've done. Pretty much. They've had to sit him out at times, even when he wanted to keep going. So it's been good. Actually, great," James said.

Those comments came before the late-practice report surfaced. Now, LeBron James has gone a step further by publicly defending Embiid's punctuality.

articles.title: David Jablonski: ‘A drive to be good’ — Hard work pays off as Springfield native reaches big leagues
articles.summary: Darren Himsworth coached Ben Ross long before he reached the big leagues with the Minnesota Twins and remembers one key ingredient that lay the foundation fo...
articles.body:
Darren Himsworth coached Ben Ross long before he reached the big leagues with the Minnesota Twins and remembers one key ingredient that lay the foundation for future success.

"The biggest thing was that he worked his tail off," Himsworth said.

The coach and player crossed paths with the Miami Valley Prospects, a summer team then based in New Carlisle. Himsworth remembers Ross, then a student at Shawnee High School, and Kyle Lane, of Xenia, keeping him at the facility for 30 to 60 minutes after practice.

"It was super late during the week," said Himsworth, a 2009 Vandalia Butler High School graduate who is the program director for the Miami Valley Prospects and also an assistant coach on Mitchell Griffiths' staff at Wittenberg. "I'm sure their parents weren't very happy about it, but we wouldn't be done with practice until 9, and I feel like I'd be walking out of the facility at like 10:15. So the drive to be good was always there."

The hard work paid off for Ross, a 2019 Springfield Shawnee High School graduate who played for the Prospects for much of his high school career. A standout career at Notre Dame College led to him being drafted by the Twins in the fifth round in 2022. He rose through the organization before earning his chance in the big leagues when rosters expanded in September.

Himsworth drove to Detroit to see Ross play in early September, and even though he didn't get into the game, he got to meet with him at the stadium.

"I congratulated him," Himsworth said. "I just asked him questions about how he was enjoying things, and he was loving it. It's a pretty surreal moment. He didn't say this, but he was probably at some point reflecting on the dream that he had when he was a kid and he and his dad were playing catch in the backyard. To see that come true, it's pretty awesome."

Ross hit .190 (4 for 21) in 10 games with two doubles, a triple, five runs scored and one RBI. Himsworth saw many of the tools Ross uses now in the three summers he coached him.

"He had great hands," Himsworth said. "He had a solid arm. He was always a super high contact hitter."

"He was little on the skinnier side in high school," Himsworth said. "The power wasn't necessarily there, but I think you always felt that once the strength got there, he might turn into something. He always ran the bases super well. I wouldn't say he was blistering fast, but sometimes the high IQ out there can overtake the speed. As he got stronger, he got faster. He was a three-plus tool player in high school. Now with the arm and the physicality and the speed, it's been fun to see him blossom into a five-tool guy."

Springfield native records first big league hits

Himsworth also coached at Wittenberg when Ross was in high school. That was his first stint with the program. He remembers Ross visiting Wittenberg before he ended up at Notre Dame College.

"I knew it was going to be a tough get with him," Himsworth said, "but I thought we had a chance. Then I had told my alma mater (Notre Dame) about him, and he got to play in front of them in the summer, and they liked him. They brought him up for a workout. I remember those guys calling me after he left, and saying, 'We think this kid's like the real deal.'"

Ross received scholarship money at Division II Notre Dame that he wouldn't have received at D-III Wittenberg.

During Ross' college career, Himsworth talked to a Texas Rangers scout about him. That scout saw Ross play at a showcase event and monitored his play during the summer with the Champion City Kings in Springfield.

Later the scout told Himsworth, "I've been following Ben Ross with the Kings for the last two weeks, and I absolutely love him."

At that point, Himsworth realized Ross had a serious chance to play professional baseball.

"He's always been a talented player — super great kid, coachable," Himsworth said. "His dad (Andy) obviously did a heck of a job coaching him growing up, really from little league until he passed him off to us in high school. And his mom, Tiffany, has been a huge piece of that, too."

Ben isn't the only athlete in his family. His sister Dani starred at Shawnee before playing D-I softball at Canisius University. His brother Joey was an All-Central Buckeye Conference performer at Shawnee as a senior in 2025 and played D-III baseball at Millikin University last season.

Himsworth also praised other coaches who impacted Ross' career in the early years, such as Rob Cassell, Jay Lewis and Eddie Meyers. Cassell coached Shawnee in Ross' first two seasons of high school baseball (2016 and 2017). Brad Olinger coached the 2018 season, and Mark Armstrong was the coach in 2019 when Ross was a senior.

"He's been around some pretty good baseball people his whole life," Himsworth said.

Himsworth joined the Rangers scouting department in 2022 just before Ross was drafted. He thought the Rangers might pick him close to the 10th round.

"We had a gathering of our old summer coaches that had coached him at my house," Himsworth said. "We were watching the draft on TV and weren't expecting him to go in the fifth round. I don't think he was either. The whole place went crazy."

In recent years, Himsworth followed Ross as he climbed the ranks in the Twins organization: from the Fort Myers Mighty Mussels in the Single-A Florida State League to the Cedar Rapids Kernels in the High-A Midwest League to the Double-A Wichita Wind Surge in the Texas League and finally this season to the Triple-A Saint Paul Saints in the International League.

Ross hit .236 with 67 home runs in five minor league seasons. He played every position but catcher.

"He was always a shortstop for us and a shortstop in college," Himsworth said, "but they used his versatility. He played so many different positions. They even pitched him down in the minors, where I think he was throwing a knuckleball in some of those games that were out of hand. At certain levels of the minors, it has taken him a little bit longer to get going, but he's always found a way. If there's one thing about him, if it's not working well, he's going to work to work his way out of it. Hopefully, he continues to get a chance and gets some sustained time at the big-league level."

articles.title: Top draft pick Gavin McKenna picks up first NHL goal, assist for Toronto against Predators
articles.summary: 1 draft pick Gavin McKenna scored his first NHL goal with the Toronto Maple Leafs on Tuesday night.McKenna scored on Nashville Predators goaltender Juuse Sar...
articles.body:
TORONTO (AP) — No. 1 draft pick Gavin McKenna scored his first NHL goal with the Toronto Maple Leafs on Tuesday night.

McKenna scored on Nashville Predators goaltender Juuse Saros in the second period of his fourth professional game. The 18-year-old took a pass from Auston Matthews, beat Saros with a high shot and then dropped to one knee in celebration at Scotiabank Arena.

McKenna also had an assist on Toronto's first goal by William Nylander for his first NHL point.

The Maple Leafs missed the playoffs for the first time in a decade last spring, and beat the draft lottery odds by winning the right to select McKenna with the first overall selection in June.

The Yukon native who played college hockey at Penn State was just one of a number of new faces to arrive in Toronto during the off season. The Maple Leafs added goaltender Sergei Bobrovsky and defenseman Darren Raddysh before the club acquired winger Kirill Marchenko a day before its regular-season opener.

McKenna, who tore up the Canadian Hockey League before spending 2025-26 in the NCAA, entered play averaging 14 minutes, 32 seconds of ice time with three shots on target and a minus-3 rating through three games.

articles.title: Why Tim Hardaway Jr. believes Giannis’ offensive ‘gravity’ will positively impact Heat
articles.summary: MIAMI – With Giannis Antetokounmpo starting a new chapter in the NBA with the Miami Heat this season, the first glimpse of how the team will operate with the...
articles.body:
MIAMI – With Giannis Antetokounmpo starting a new chapter in the NBA with the Miami Heat this season, the first glimpse of how the team will operate with the two-time MVP came in Saturday's 128-105 win over the Toronto Raptors in the preseason opener. As other newcomers join the Heat with Antetokounmpo, like Tim Hardaway Jr., the veteran guard explains a certain aspect about the big man that will lead to major success with Miami.

In the preseason win, Antetokounmpo would log 14 minutes of play, recording nine points on three-for-three shooting from the field, three of four from the free-throw line, to go along with seven assists and four rebounds. What stood out the most was the way he initiated offense through his playmaking ability and attracting defenders while doing so.

Hardaway had a nice night of his own, leading the team with 14 points on four-for-four shooting from the field, making all three from beyond the arc. Speaking to ClutchPoints on Monday, he cited Antetokounmpo's "gravity" as being a trait that adds a key layer to the team.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

"We make the extra pass, and then we go from there and live with the results," Hardaway said. "But it was very fun and very exciting for the most part. Very fast. Guy takes up a lot of space. His gravity is insane. So just still learning as the preseason goes on. He's gonna be out there with a lot of different lineups. So we just gotta understand what we're dealing with. But all in all, solid performance."

Heat's Klay Thompson impressed with Giannis Antetokounmpo's passing

It's important to note that the basis for the offensive performance from the Heat is based on one preseason game where Antetokounmpo played 14 minutes, but it was still a positive first effort. Miami would record 41 points in the first quarter and 76 points in the first half, which also showcased its fast pace, which the Heat led the league in last season.

For another newcomer, Klay Thompson was impressed by Antetokounmpo's playmaking.

"My thoughts are how I was so impressed by Giannis' playmaking," Thompson said. "I mean, I know he's a great passer, but wow, he gets so many great looks. I'm going to be on the receiving end of so many of those, so I'm not worried about my field goal attempts or shooting efficiency as much in the preseason. I'm more just focused on getting a grasp of this offensive system, defensive system, and being in the right spots. So I've been in this league a long time. I'm going to be able to have great looks."

Heat's Giannis Antetokounmpo has "dopamine hits" when getting assists

Antetokounmpo's passing and playmaking would even garner the attention of head coach Erik Spoelstra, who compared him to legendary point guard Magic Johnson. When hearing that, Antetokounmpo was no doubt flattered, though candidly saying that he believes he's "far away" from Johnson, citing how he gets "dopamine hits" when recording assists.

"It's a great compliment. I think I'm far away from Magic Johnson, if not the best point guard to ever play this game," Antetokounmpo said Monday. "But it's always fun to me. I think every coach that I've been around, they always say the same thing…Like, 'Oh, actually, I didn't know that Giannis could pass the ball.' I've had J-Kidd [Jason Kidd] say that in the past. Coach Bud [Mike Budenholzer], Doc Rivers, now Coach Spo [Spoelstra]. So for me, I take pride in making plays for myself and for my teammates."

"It's almost like I get little dopamine hits when I'm able to get in the lane and find the open guy for a three or for an easy two," Antetokounmpo continued. "I've always enjoyed that, and now I have the opportunity within our offense that it's kind of easy. The spacing is easy. Everybody's moving. I think it's kind of easier for me to find those guys. I'm looking forward to guys making shots, being open, and me trying to deliver the ball as well as I can."

At any rate, Antetokounmpo will continue to build chemistry with the Heat as the home preseason opener is on Thursday against the New Orleans Pelicans, which is ahead of the first game of the regular season on Oct. 21 against the Minnesota Timberwolves.

articles.title: Bills Face Strong Tyreek Hill Prediction as NFL Comeback Looms
articles.summary: The Bills have been identified as a top landing spot for wide receiver Tyreek Hill, should he pass on the Kansas City Chiefs. The post Bills Face Strong Tyre...
articles.body:
The Buffalo Bills could have a chance to supercharge their passing game by adding a longtime rival.

Former Kansas City Chiefs and Miami Dolphins wide receiver Tyreek Hill is nearing his NFL return after a long injury rehab, with one insider pegging the Bills as a top potential landing spot. The Bills have gotten some spotty production from their wide receiving corps so far, and Hill could be a proven target for quarterback Josh Allen.

Bills Could Swoop in to Snag Tyreek Hill

In an article breaking down the top three potential landing spots for Hill, SI.com writer Ethen Hutton suggested the Bills are near the top of the list. He suggested that the Chiefs — who are reeling from a pair of injuries to their wide receiving corps — might be the only team ahead of the Bills on Hill's list.

While there may not be much competition for the Chiefs, the Bills could be waiting in the wings if the two sides can't reach a deal, Hutton suggested.

"Aside from the Chiefs, I feel the Buffalo Bills have the best chance to land Hill, though I don't expect him to land anywhere besides Kansas City at this point," Hutton wrote. "The Bills fit Hill's preference for cold-weather football, per his latest viral tweet, and present a favorable landing spot as a legitimate contender in the AFC. Buffalo's top target DJ Moore is dealing with a shoulder injury, which could elevate the Bills' odds to add the five-time All-Pro."

While the Chiefs are dealing with injuries to Rashee Rice and Tyquan Thornton, the Bills have some dinged-up receivers of their own. DJ Moore was knocked out of Sunday's loss to the New England Patriots with a persistent shoulder issue, and Keon Coleman has been playing through an injury of his own.

The Bills have already made some roster moves this season, though their focus appears to be on the back end of the defense. The team signed 25-year-old cornerback A.J. Woods to the practice squad on Tuesday, filling a spot that became vacant after the Arizona Cardinals poached offensive tackle Jedrick Wills Jr.

"Woods was an undrafted free agent out of the University of Pittsburgh in 2024 by the Washington Commanders ," the team noted. "He was later released and signed to the Philadelphia Eagles practice squad that season, becoming a Super Bowl champion at Super Bowl LIX.

The Bills added that Woods could bring some speed and versatility to the secondary.

"At 5-foot-11 and 195 pounds, Woods joins the Bills' defensive back room as another young, versatile piece," the team noted. "At his pro day back in 2024, he ran a 4.35-second 40-yard dash with a 6.56-second three-cone drill and 16 reps on the bench press."

articles.title: “That's The Sprint Car Driver” – HMS Protégé Distances Himself From Stock Car Stars After Fearless Las Vegas Wall-Ride
articles.summary: On the last lap at Las Vegas Motor Speedway on Saturday, Carson Kvapil thought he would be sailing into the NASCAR O’Reilly Auto Parts Series championship le...
articles.body:
On the last lap at Las Vegas Motor Speedway on Saturday, Carson Kvapil thought he would be sailing into the NASCAR O'Reilly Auto Parts Series championship lead. That was before he saw a Hendrick Motorsports Chevrolet bounce off the wall and zoom past him full throttle. The JR Motorsports car finished second by a mere 0.287 seconds.

Corey Day, in the No. 17 HMS Chevy, was the most dominant driver on the day, and he walked away from Vegas with 75 points. He won stage 1, finished second at the end of stage two, and led 136 of the 201 laps. Day pulled off a move most drivers wouldn't, and for that he thanked his sprint car foundations.

"For me, I know what I'm doing in a late-race scenario like that," Day told the media, including FloRacing . On pavement, not as much. I think, honestly, a little bit of sprint car came out in me, hitting the fence, running the fence, all that sort of thing. That's a sprint car driver and me just not lifting and getting everything I can out of it."

"I think a stock car guy in my position probably would have made some different decisions there late in that race," Day added. "But it worked out, so I'm not going to think about other ways I could have done it."

Day moved into stock cars and began racing on asphalt in 2024. At his core, he is a sprint car driver, and the move that he pulled to get past Kvapil on the final lap was something straight out of the sprint car driver's playbook.

On the last 13 laps, as Day closed in and lapped traffic, Kvapil was right behind him, and the JRM No. 1 and HMS No. 17 swapped the lead four times. Kvapil finished with 3 laps led, all of which came during the closing 13 laps.

On the final lap, Day was running the outside line, neck and neck to Kvapil. The HMS No. 17 hit the wall with its rear right on the exit of turn two but kept his foot on the throttle.

Day caught his car and kept putting the pressure on Kvapil. Coming out of turns three and four, Day kept running closer to the outside wall and bumped twice. The second bump sent him flying ahead. And at no point did he give up the throttle. Straightening on the final stretch, Day used the momentum off the wall to get ahead and cut in front of Kvapil, ensuring the HMS got past the finish line first.

Three wall bumps on the final lap, most stock car drivers would have left the car or the momentum they were trying to build. But for Day, it was the kind of wall-hugging racing that he had growing up racing sprint cars at dirt tracks.

Even Kenny Wallace pointed to Day's brilliance that made the NOAPS race look like a complete spectacle in Vegas. Wallace compared Day to the HMS star who played a crucial role in getting him into the Hendrick pipeline.

"Last night, Kvapil had that race won. And that damn Corey Day, if I were to turn the volume down and watch the race, I'd have sworn that was Kyle Larson in that car." Wallace said. "And it was Kyle Larson that told Rick Hendrick, 'You gotta hire Corey Day. He's the next me.' And now it's finally coming to fruition."

Day is already locked into his current No. 17 HMS seat in NOAPS for 2027. Hendrick sees him as a long-term prospect, and the 20-year-old will get his first taste of top-tier stock car racing in the Cup series next year.

Day is scheduled to run 5 to 6 races next year in a Spire Motorsports Chevrolet. HMS has four Cup cars, but they also have four full-time Cup drivers for 2027. The aim is to get Day ready to eventually go full-time in the Cup Series, which is why HMS will ease him in through their technical alliance with Spire. Although the schedule isn't confirmed yet, the races are supposed to be those in the mid to latter half of the season.

But the timeline on Day's rookie Cup season is still unclear. Alex Bowman has already announced that 2027 will be his last full season in the No. 48 Chevrolet as he plans to retire from Cup racing.

Connor Zilisch, who is having a rough rookie season at Trackhouse Racing, has already been confirmed as the next No.48 driver. The other three drivers, Kyle Larson, Chase Elliott, and William Byron, are already locked in long-term, so neither of those seats is likely to free up anytime soon.

But Day's progress is one that HMS will monitor closely, hoping that he can work as the perfect substitute driver if and when required. HMS felt that requirement this year when Bowman was ruled out from four races after being diagnosed with vertigo.

While the eyes are on his long-term future at HMS, Day will have his own sights set on the present season. With just five races remaining, Day will be hoping he has another win at the very least to have a shot at the title. Currently, he sits 41 points off leader Sheldon Creed.

articles.title: Sale struggles and bats cold as Braves fall to Dodgers
articles.summary: Sale struggled by his standards and had little run support in loss
articles.body:
The Atlanta Braves took on the Dodgers tonight in a pivotal game that would give them the 2-1 lead in the NLDS. Chris Sale took on Yoshinobu Yamamoto. The last time these two faced of Sale pitched a complete game shutout and the Braves won 1-0.

The first inning looked great for Sale. He gave up a leadoff single to Betts and Ha-Seong Kim committed an error, but Sale struck out Freeman, Smith and Ohtani. Yamamoto answered with a great inning of his own, striking out the first two hitters and getting Olson to groundout.

In the second, Tucker singled and stole second, but Sale struck out every other hitter he faced. Harris singled in the second for the first base runner for the Braves, but it was the only offense. The third inning got dramatic. Betts singled, but then Dubón robbed Freddie Freeman of a HR.

After a Teoscar Hernández fly out, Smith singled and then Ohtani reached on catcher's interference to load the bases. Sale was able to get Rojas to line out to end the top of the inning with no damage done. The Braves had zero offense in the third.

The fourth is where it started to fall apart for Sale. Pages singled. Tucker lined out, but then postseason legend Enrique Hernández hit a two-run shot to give the Dodgers a lead. Betts grounded out, but then Freeman added a HR of his own to make the score 3-0. Fortunately, Teoscar Hernández had a 108.4 MPH fly out to end the top of the fourth. Matt Olson singled, but it was the only offense in the fourth for the Braves.

Sale stayed in to pitch the fifth and retired the side to include a strikeout of Will Smith. It looked like the Braves might get some momentum in the fifth with a Dubón single followed by a Thomas single. Riley struck out, but then Tellez pinch hit for Kim and walked to load the bases. Baldwin grounded out to score a run, but then Acuña grounded out himself to end the inning.

Dylan Dodd came in to pitch the sixth. Sale ended his start with 5.0 innings with three earned runs, seven hits, zero walks, and seven strikeouts. Pages had a single, but then Dodd sat down the rest to include two strikeouts. Unfortunately, the Braves did not do any better as they were retired in order.

Dylan Lee came in to pitch the seventh. He has been struggling lately, but it did make sense to bring him in here. He was able to retire the side to keep the game close. The bottom of the lineup looked like the bottom of the lineup for the Braves as they were sat down in order again in the seventh.

Brent Suter came in to pitch the eighth. An interesting choice. He walked Ohtani on seven pitches. Rojas then tweaked something and was replaced by Edman who popped up. Suter then prevented anymore offense. Tanner Scott then came in to replace Yamamoto. Hicklen struck out and Baldwin grounded out. Ronald Acuña then walked on five pitches. Olson was able to get Scott to pitch six pitches, but struck out. This left the Braves three outs to tie it up.

Raisel Iglesias came in to pitch the ninth. He was able to induce a pop up from Hernández after falling to a 3-0 count. He then struck out Mookie Betts on eight pitches. This brought up Freddie Freeman who walked on sox pitches. Max Muncy pinch hit for Teoscar Hernández. Muncy struck out on three pitches.

Edwin Díaz came in to pitch the ninth. Ozzie Albies has been one of the best hitters on the team this postseason and continued with a double to lead off the ninth. Harris made Díaz work, but ultimately grounded out on eight pitches and moved Albies to third. Mauricio Dubón flies out to right and it was not far enough to score the run. Mike Yastrzemski replaced Lane Thomas as the last chance. He then grounded out to end the game, putting the Braves at a big disadvantage moving forward.

Next game is at home with Tyler Mahle on the mound with a win or go home game. The bats were cold as ever, and will need to wake up against Glasnow to stay alive.

articles.title: Watch: Messi scores for Argentina in final international game
articles.summary: Lionel Messi couldn't say farewell to the Argentina national team without a goal.
articles.body:
Lionel Messi couldn't say farewell to the Argentina national team without a goal.

In his final international match, the Argentina legend scored from the penalty spot in the 71st minute against Benin on Tuesday, Oct. 6 .

Messi's goal made it 3-0 on the night, and ignited the sold-out crowd at Estadio Monumental in Buenos Aires.

Argentina went up 2-0 with second-half goals from Nicolás Otamendi and Nico Paz, both of which were assisted by Messi.

The home side then drew a penalty, and Messi stepped up and buried a shot to his right.

It would be the final goal of the match, as Argentina sent Messi off with a 3-0 victory.

Messi announced his international retirement in August, but Argentina called the 39-year-old up one final time to get a send-off in front of his home fans.

It was an emotional night in Buenos Aires as Messi was honored for an international career that spanned more than two decades.

Messi finishes his international career as Argentina's record scorer with 126 goals and record appearance-maker with 208 caps.

The Golden State Valkyries have to win two more games against the Las Vegas Aces to reach the WNBA Finals, but the schedule at Chase Center appears crowded in October.

As the highest seed remaining, the Valkyries would retain home-court advantage in the best-of-seven series with Games 1 and 2 on Oct. 17 and 19 at Chase Center.

A Doja Cat concert scheduled at the arena for Oct. 19 at 7:30 p.m. would pose a conflict. But the Valkyries said the concert would be moved to a contingency date.

articles.title: Michigan TE Zack Marshall apologizes for texts ripping OC Jason Beck
articles.summary: The Wolverines tight end what's sorry for his actions.
articles.body:
Michigan Wolverines tight end Zack Marshall apologized Tuesday after text messages from him criticizing offensive coordinator Jason Beck were leaked on social media, following the Wolverines' 20-14 loss to Minnesota.

The Michigan football program has endured a turbulent 10 months under new coach Kyle Whittingham, and the frustration inside the program appears to be boiling over. The turmoil began with the firing of head coach Sherrone Moore after an inappropriate relationship with a staffer came to light. The situation escalated months later when Moore was arrested on stalking and home invasion charges. He ultimately accepted a plea bargain in the spring.

Michigan's ensuing coaching search was rocky, but the program eventually landed Whittingham, hiring him away from Utah. His tenure, however, has gotten off to a disastrous start. Whittingham's first game produced an ugly win, and Michigan has struggled even more since, going winless in Big Ten play and falling out of the national rankings.

The Wolverines' problems have extended to the offense, where former five-star quarterback Bryce Underwood has struggled to live up to expectations. His performance has become a growing concern, with questions emerging about whether Michigan should consider benching him.

Now, frustration among the players is becoming public.

Marshall, a senior tight end who was part of Jim Harbaugh's 2023 national championship team, expressed his displeasure with Beck in a private group chat that leaked. Marshall alleged that Beck told the team's tight ends that none of them were valuable to the offense and added that "this offense sucks." With Michigan ranking 105th nationally in points per game, the criticism has struck a nerve. After the screenshots spread, Marshall took responsibility for his comments and apologized on X.

Marshall caught 16 passes for 199 yards last season but has yet to record a reception in five games under Whittingham and Beck.

Michigan now enters its bye week with plenty to fix. When the Wolverines return, they will host Penn State in a matchup between two of the Big Ten's most disappointing teams—and one that could reveal just how deep Michigan's problems have become.

articles.title: Cal QB Jaron-Keawe Sagapolutele in concussion protocol; status for Saturday unclear
articles.summary: Cal quarterback Jaron-Keawe Sagapolutele, who left last Saturday's game with concussion symptoms, is "day-to-day" for this Saturday. Also, Cal GM Ron Rivera...
articles.body:
Cal quarterback Jaron-Keawe Sagapolutele is in concussion protocol after being held out of the second half of the Bears' 39-31 loss at UNLV on Saturday, coach Tosh Lupoi said Tuesday.

Sagapolutele is "day-to-day" ahead of Saturday's homecoming game in Berkeley against Virginia Tech, Lupoi said.

Lupoi recounted the play on which the sophomore quarterback suffered the concussion, saying the manner he was knocked down "whiplashed" Sagapolutele's head into the ground. Lupoi then reiterated what he told reporters after the UNLV loss: Sagapolutele was medically cleared to return to play after halftime but Lupoi made the call to hold him out.

"Jaron had a concussion in the game" against UNLV, Lupoi said. "He was wobbling off the field; obviously, everybody saw that. So we pulled him out of the game. I was actually told he was cleared and ready to go in the game at halftime. I was very uncomfortable with that.

"The last thing I'm going to do is jeopardize that young man's future and his life. … There were some symptoms there possibly. And so no matter what, I'm not going to jeopardize that young man and anybody on this team. Just based off of my human instinct, based off what I saw, ain't nobody gonna go out there. "

It's unclear how or why Sagapolutele, who appeared shaken when he rejoined the huddle after the hit, was initially cleared to return.

Per the NCAA's Concussion Safety Protocol checklist, available on the organization's website, student-athletes who display signs/symptoms/behaviors consistent with a concussion must be evaluated by an athletic trainer or team physician (or physician designee) with concussion experience and cannot return to play if a concussion is suspected. And as required by the NCAA's Independent Medical Care Legislation, team physicians and athletic trainers shall have unchallengeable autonomous authority to determine medical management and return-to-play decisions for all student-athletes.

Sagapolutele "along with all the other players in concussion - we have an extremely strict protocol here," Lupoi said. "They go through multiple testing every day, and there's a protocol that we follow, and so I'm going to follow that, and I will go off the medical professional's opinion."

Sagapolutele was 19-for-27 for 195 yards and a touchdown against UNLV. Backup Jackson Brousseau was 19-for-32 for 200 yards and two touchdowns.

Lupoi said Sagapolutele did not participate in the full-contact portion practice Tuesday, but was present. According to the NCAA's Concussion Safety Protocol, student-athletes must undergo a six-step management plan supervised by a health care provider with expertise in concussions to be cleared to return to play.

Rivera on offense: Team general manager Ron Rivera backed Lupoi over his decision to change offensive playcallers during the UNLV game.

Lupoi said the Bears had multiple coaches handling offensive playcalling responsibilities through the first half at UNLV before he made the call to give the duties to pass game coordinator Pat McCann after the first possession of the second half.

Cal scored 24 points in the second half after scoring seven in the first half.

"Drawing up things on the sideline, getting on the iPad, maniac energy of trying to put things in, put a receiver in the backfield, run a play that we did not practice a single time for an explosive touchdown - Pat McCann dressed all that up," Lupoi said of wide receiver Cooper Perry's 53-yard wheel route touchdown at the 4:40 mark in the third quarter.

Including Perry's TD, the Bears scored 24 points after Lupoi made the swap, a sign of encouragement for a Cal offense that has been lackluster this season with offensive coordinator Jordan Somerville on the headset.

"I think it just shows that (Lupoi's) looking for answers, which is great," Rivera said. "He's trying to be aggressive in terms of finding those answers, and really just trying to show the players that he's willing to do what he needs to do to give ourselves a chance to win. If you continue to do the same thing, is that insanity? He keeps getting the same results, and I think that's kind of what he's alluding to is that he felt he had to do that. Our initial play caller is a young playcaller (Somerville) who's got a lot to learn still. Very good football coach, understands the game, but he's got some things to learn."

The rotating door at offensive playcaller is a sign of the urgency from Lupoi, Rivera, and the Cal football program feels sitting at 2-3 on the season. But while Bears know this first season in a new era has not gone as well as they had hoped, Rivera maintained his confidence in what Cal is building, pointing to how the Bears have been in these games all the way to the bitter end.

"The potential," Rivera answered when asked what he's seen from these first five games that gives him confidence the Bears can turn this season around.

"You see the plays that they make, you see the things that they've done to put themselves in position (to win), and that's where you feel really good about who they are. They're working their tails off. They're doing the things that they need to do, and at the same time, they're trying to be student-athletes. I think it takes a lot. I really do, and to see them come out, and I agree with what (Lupoi) said too. They're going to fight to the end."

Brooklyn Nets rookie Mikel Brown Jr. is progressing in his recovery from a sprained left ankle that has limited him during the first week of training camp, coach Jordi Fernández said.

Brown sustained the injury last month and has been limited to non-contact drills and other related on-court work with the team. He was ruled out of their exhibition opener on Tuesday, along with fellow rookie Joshua Jefferson (back).

The sixth overall pick is taking part in more activity and was recently allowed to begin some contact work with the coaching staff, according to Sharif Phillips-Keaton of Nets Wire . The team hopes he can suit up in one of its three remaining preseason games.

Brown played only 21 games last season at Louisville because of a back injury that sidelined him midseason and during the postseason. He still became the Cardinals' highest-drafted player since Felton Spencer was selected sixth overall in 1990.

The 6-foot-5 Brown debuted with the Nets in summer league, averaging 15 points, four assists, 1.5 rebounds and 1.2 steals while shooting 34.6% from 3-point range in four games. He finished in double figures in each appearance, including a 20-point performance on July 10.

Brown believes summer league helped him learn the playbook and some of the concepts and coverages the team will deploy this season. While he isn't certain when he can return, Brown is busy observing his teammates and studying film.

articles.title: Meteorologist warns Alabama-Georgia could be moved due to hurricane
articles.summary: The No. 2 Georgia Bulldogs are headed to Tuscaloosa, Alabama, on Saturday to take on the Alabama Crimson Tide in a showdown of SEC title contenders. Unfortun...
articles.body:
The No. 2 Georgia Bulldogs are headed to Tuscaloosa, Alabama, on Saturday to take on the Alabama Crimson Tide in a showdown of SEC title contenders. Unfortunately, it sounds like there's a chance that severe weather could impact the contest.

One prominent meteorologist is suggesting that the game could be impacted by a potential hurricane that could even result in the contest being moved or rescheduled.

While it's still very early, current models project that Isaias, which is currently classified as a tropical depression, could strike the Gulf Coast south of Mobile, Ala., at some point Saturday, which could obviously interfere with the game in Tuscaloosa.

"Tropical Depression Nine [Isaias] has developed in the southwestern Gulf and is forecast to intensify into a hurricane over the next 48 to 72 hours," the National Weather Service office in Birmingham wrote on its website Tuesday afternoon . "Some model uncertainties still exist in regards to timing, intensity, and exact track, so refinements to this forecast are likely. Most impacts to Central Alabama will be felt in the form of gusty winds and steady rainfall Friday into Saturday. Continue to check the latest forecasts from official sources. Start considering preparations for power outages and flooding."

The SEC has already issued a statement indicating that the conference is monitoring the situation ahead of this weekend's slate of college football games.

While it's still too early to know the exact strength and direction of the storm, prominent Alabama-based meteorologist James Spann has warned that moving the game is "clearly on the table."

"The idea of moving the game, it's on the table," Spann told AL.com's Michael Casagrande on Tuesday . "I'm saying it's clearly on the table. It would be a nightmare for everybody involved. But if we do get a Category 1, Category 2 hurricane coming right up Mobile Bay [on] Saturday morning, I don't know if you wouldn't be playing that game in Tuscaloosa that you've got the chance of winds gusting to 50 miles an hour, torrential rain and the chance of isolated tornadoes on top of everything else."

It will certainly be interesting to see how the storm continues to develop.

articles.title: USANA inks deal to become Utah Athletics’ nutrition partner, adds more than 500 Ute athletes to sponsor roster
articles.summary: As part of the partnership, Salt Lake City-based USANA will add more than 500 athletes across all of Utah’s 19 sports to its sponsorship roster.
articles.body:
USANA is now the official vitamin, mineral and nutrition partner of the University of Utah, the company announced in an event at Rice-Eccles Stadium on Tuesday.

As part of the partnership, Salt Lake City-based USANA will add more than 500 athletes across all of Utah's 19 sports to its sponsorship roster.

"USANA has been a Utah-based company for 35 years and we felt it was super important to support our home community where we operate and have hundreds of employees that work and operate here," said Brent Neidig, USANA's chief commercial officer.

"We actually have hundreds of employees that have graduated from the University of Utah. To us, it's a natural fit. The University of Utah excels in excellence and they have a phenomenal program here. We feel it's a great opportunity for us to provide our world-class supplements to the program.

USANA and Utah have been discussing the partnership for the past "year or so," per Neidig.

As part of the deal, USANA will provide Utah Athletics with its line of nutritional supplements.

"Utah Athletics' partnership with USANA is a game-changer for our student-athletes and our Performance Nutrition program," said Meredith Price, Utah Assistant A.D. for Performance Nutrition, in a press release.

"Our team of dietitians work individually with student-athletes to optimize their nutrition for performance, recovery and health. Having access to high-quality, third-party sport-tested supplements from USANA allows us to keep health and safety at the forefront of our recommendations."

Utah and USANA will also provide athletes the opportunity to work with USANA Foundation, which has a goal of ending malnutrition. USANA will also help connect University of Utah athletes with youth sports organizations.

"One other thing that we're very excited about is the opportunity to incorporate the athletes here at the university with our foundation, which is engaged in providing food and meals to children in need all throughout the state here," Neidig said.

USANA's sponsorship of Utah Athletics will primarily focus on providing athletes with products, but there will be NIL opportunities for athletes.

"A product-first partnership, and that's how we structure all of our deals around the world. We have over 4,000 elite and Olympic athletes that consume our product. Whenever we start a conversation with a new organization or team, we always focus on the product first. That is the primary bulk of our partnership, which is providing products to the athletes here," Neidig said.

"Naturally, there is some other additions to the partnership, a little bit of NIL money."

articles.title: DAZN replaces Max Kellerman with Mario Lopez as ‘Inside the Ring’ host
articles.summary: DAZN announced Tuesday morning that Saved By The Bell and Extra alum Mario Lopez would be joining its Inside the Ring show. What it didn’t mention was that f...
articles.body:
DAZN announced Tuesday morning that Saved By The Bell and Extra alum Mario Lopez would be joining its Inside the Ring show.

What it didn't mention was that former host Max Kellerman and analyst LeSean McCoy wouldn't be there to greet him. According to Ryan Glasspiegel of Front Office Sports , they will not be returning for the second season of the boxing show.

Boxing insider Mike Coppinger announced Monday that he would return to the program, noting it would now stream twice a week on DAZN Boxing and Ring Magazine's YouTube channels. That follows last week's report from Total Boxing that Saudi official Turki Alalshikh has agreed to sell a controlling interest in Ring Magazine to DAZN .

According to a write-up in Ring , Lopez will be the show's new full-time host, teaming with Coppinger and a rotating panel of analysts. The longtime actor is a major boxing enthusiast, serving as a guest color commentator for boxing events and co-hosting a boxing podcast, The 3 Knockdown Rule , with Ring contributor Steve Kim.

Per FOS, the change won't impact Kellerman's role calling matches for Zuffa Boxing , a joint venture between the Saudi Public Investment Fund and TKO.

It's been a tough week for the former ESPN talking head, who was slammed over comments he made about the recently announced Tyson Fury-Anthony Joshua fight and accused of being a mouthpiece for Alalshikh's camp in their public feud with Dana White.
